artworks.title: Perseus and Andromeda
artworks.description: Matham's engraving after Goltzius stages the Ethiopian crisis Cepheus could not avert: Andromeda bound for the monster after Cassiopeia's boast — the king as the helpless father at the edge of the rescue.

artworks.title: Andromeda Mosaic (Zeugma)
artworks.description: A floor mosaic from Zeugma (Gaziantep Museum) returns to the Ethiopian royal myth Cepheus rules: Andromeda's ordeal as provincial Roman floor spectacle — the king's household story carried east along the Euphrates.

films.title: Clash of the Titans
films.description: Davis's film keeps Cepheus as the king forced to offer Andromeda — the Ethiopian throne bent by oracle and sea-monster until Perseus rewrites the sentence.

popCulture.title: Cepheus (constellation)
popCulture.description: The Ethiopian king was placed among the circumpolar stars beside Cassiopeia and Andromeda — a faint northern constellation that still names the father who exposed his daughter to the sea.

popCulture.title: Cepheus (father of Andromeda)
popCulture.description: King of Aethiopia and father of Andromeda — the mortal ruler whose wife's boast and whose daughter's chains define the Perseus cycle.
